[**I Love You, Man**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#i-love-you-man)

11\. 20 – 01\. 15. 2021

- [Bernadette Despujols](https://spinelloprojects.com/artist/bernadette-despujols/)

In I Love You, Man Bernadette Despujols paints the closest men in her circle. The paintings are a departure from her usual depictions of women in paintings. In previous paintings of fully nude women, Despujols positioned herself as the subject of her paintings although they were portraits of anonymous unconscious women sourced from pornography made by men. Holding the belief that to be a woman makes other people uncomfortable and ultimately poses a threat to men she turns her gaze and paints the cishet men in her life: friends, lovers, family. Despujols uses the portraiture of her male subjects to experience her relationships with deeper intimacy. Objectification and intersubjectivity (the relation or intersection between people's cognitive perspectives) ebbs and flows between the painter and the painted. She objectifies the men in the paintings at times, focusing solely on one body part or their bare skin and bodies, but the men pose for the pictures with awareness and dignity. Nothing is stolen from them; Despujols may want to position these men ironically as muses but the truth is she defeats the irony of it with pure affinity and care towards the people she paints, leaving the men to decide what they want to wear and show of themselves. In the act of portraiture she experiences the vulnerability of these men through their quiet shyness or awkwardness with themselves, ways that would otherwise challenge the presumed status quo of manhood: tough, aggressive, aloof, qualities of patriarchy that, to Despujols, imprison both men and women in a cycle of violence. The paintings are formally infused with skewed perspectives, foreground and background foibles, and blank, paintless spaces furthering the playfulness she captures by being around the men she loves.

[**They Dreamt of Us**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#they-dreamt-of-us)

11\. 20 – 01\. 15. 2022

- [Reginald O'Neal](https://spinelloprojects.com/artist/reginald-oneal/)

Spinello Projects presents _They Dreamt of Us_ by Reginald O’Neal. Building upon his debut exhibition at the gallery, _At the Feet of Mountains_, O’Neal continues his practice of translating his embodied experience into realistic paintings. The exhibition features a suite of new works of an ongoing series representing portraits and still-lives that reflect the artist’s distinct perspective of life, on view at the Gesamtkunstwerk Building located at 2930 NW 7th Avenue.

O’Neal’s influences primarily derive from the late impressionist painter, Joaquin Sorolla. O’Neal paints with the same drive to capture his visual field, which includes intimate portrayals of his family and community, and the objects and spaces they own. These paintings render specific scenes that express a deep affect of reverence and veneration for quotidian people, places, and things. O’Neal’s perspective comes precisely from his standing point as his means of documenting and sharing tangible vignettes of what he sees.

These works provide detailed impressions of present and past realities of people in a sense of place. Nature, childhood, fatherhood, motherhood, and adulthood, are all reflected in these works with quiet stillness and are manifested in relation to the poetic tension of displacement, self-expression, and bondage. A suite of paintings depicts six portraits of persons of varying degrees in relation to the artist, including one painting of a Golden Trumpet tree. O’Neal takes pleasure in convincing others of the beauty in the world as a means of shifting perspectives towards a positive appreciation for life. Each painting is intended to show the subject in their most pure, natural, and honest form, yet the details of each subject give context to who this person is and what they represent or where they come from.

Each painting is its own visual story but they all connect in their ability to compose the beauty of the past, present, and the continuous. The questions of what and who is of value, what and who is consistent, and how that shapes us is posed in this presentation of documentary paintings.

[**As Flesh to Land**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#as-flesh-to-land)

10\. 02 – 11\. 06. 2021

- Mateo Nava

Spinello Projects is proud to present _As Flesh to Land_, the debut solo gallery exhibition by Mexican-American Miami-based artist Mateo Nava. The exhibition, spanning two floors, features installations of wall pinned, cut-out paintings created between 2019-2021. Exhibition on view at the Gesamtkunstwerk Building located at 2930 NW 7th Avenue, from October 2 — November 6, by appointment only.

Mateo Nava maps out sensations, memories, and intangible experiences of migration through the creation of large, layered cut-out paintings that use the body and plants to express the alienation bodies, land, and spirits endure. Beads, plastic gems, fragments of printed fabric, and sewing notions are layered and layered on the surface of the paintings. Nava intertwines the imagery of blood vessels, roots and vines, and nets and tributaries as symbols of bloodlines and history. 

Mangrove roots provide protection to fish just like our homes do for us, the pierced poppy bulb seeps out droplets of opium extract, a concise metaphor for the blood and tears shed over the drug trade, and the companion plants of corn, beans, and squash not only lay the framework for the staple diets of Mesoamericans but also lay the framework for their cosmogony. 

Violent lines such as chain links, barbed wires, thorns, nets, and imaginary state borders also appear in the works entangled among body parts and flora. In every work a body shows up and to Nava it represents a “body-place”. To him the body does not inhabit a place as much as a place inhabits the body and thus the dismembered body-place manifests as a symbol for the land; they are found continuously floating through the works. These disembodied parts interact with one another, moving in a flow, praying or seeking shelter.

[**Collective Journal Vol. 2**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#collective-journal-vol-2-curated-by-yi-chin-hsieh)

06\. 27 – 07\. 31. 2021

- Yi Chin Hsieh

Spinello Projects' The Annex, is proud to host The Collective Journal project, a series of exhibitions curated by Yi Chin Hsieh. The exhibition project gathers artworks within concepts of archiving, collection, and diaristic expression in different aspects of artists’ practices, on view through July 31st at Gesamtkunstwerk Building located at 2930 NW 7th Ave. The exhibition is open to the public and by appointment (Wed - Sat) -- schedule your appointment **[here](https://spinelloprojects.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=bdff9d4f3cd4095b8bfc6d528&id=9d475b48fa&e=4ecdbcccba)**.

_Collective Journal Vol. 2: Visible Meditations_ features “non-material” collections by four Miami-based artists: Chris Friday, Anna Goraczko, Juan Requena, and Ronald Sanchez. Their works are inspired by abstract concepts such as time, collective memories, and environmental concerns.

Juan Requena’s _Untitled_ (Plastic bag quilt) demonstrates his life and cultural experience in Mumbai, India from 2012 to 2019. The quilt is made of our most familiar daily waste: plastic bags. Requena’s practice has always surrounded the archival aspect of objects and the production process. His artwork resonates with the modern urban lifestyle and weaves his days back in India together. Similar to collecting memories, _Supplement Archive_ by Chris Friday explores identity and black culture through a lens of desire and longing. Friday relies heavily on information online, accumulating people’s reactions and behaviors toward pop culture and shared experiences. Sanchez’s installation displays collected objects he used for production: empty paint cans, can lids, brushes, and more industrial materials. His work _Lid #_, presents the process of art-making. By assembling the creative moments from both the perspectives of the maker and the viewer, Sanchez turns process documentation into the artwork itself. Lastly, Goraczko gathered random materials from her old house to make prints as documentation of her connection with her inheritance. Interested in discovering the family history, the artist started to assemble objects and notes she found in the house she grew up in. Her work _Ascended Edits_ is a proof of self-identity and a collection of intimate storytelling.

[**Day In, Day Out**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#day-in-day-out)

06\. 27 – 07\. 31. 2021

- [Clara Varas](https://spinelloprojects.com/artist/clara-varas/)

Spinello Projects is proud to present _Day In, Day Out_, a solo exhibition by Cuban-born Miami-based artist Clara Varas. The exhibition, spanning two rooms, features painting and assemblage, on view at the Gesamtkunstwerk Building located at 2930 NW 7th Avenue through July 31, by appointment only. This will be her third solo exhibition with the gallery.

In Clara Varas’ latest exhibition _Day In, Day Out_ she uses detritus from her surroundings to create a visual understanding of the intersectionality of the abject landscape. Marine, metal, and “fashion” are industries that surround the artist’s studio. This is the abject landscape—it is blighted, culturally rich, highly textured and layered, somehow forgotten but completely essential. Here, ‘home’ includes it’s displacement and who it makes someone. Time bears down on all objects used in the compositions. The body is a machine working in tandem and dependent on all that which was once not trash. What was once domestic, then became urban waste, and now exists in a still life or displaced composition.

Metal scrap yards and freight shipping empires on the banks of the Miami River, the now wasted and polluted wild waterway, obscure fashion strip malls, and the tropicality of the Latin American diaspora all obscurely collide in Varas’ mark making. Varas freezes this specific place and time, grabbing at its contradictions and details and places it in an abstraction of a still life. Objects assigned to genders or that allude to our bodies are constantly expanding their meaning and usage. Vara paints with these objects in space, and in that, records an engagement between herself, her neighbors, and where they live. Varas is moved by the immediacy of stuff; the personal becomes the collective, especially when someone’s things get somehow abandoned on the streets. Abstraction is materialized by hard and soft objects in works that teeter the line between totem and heap. Considering the unnoticed labor input by the people working in the area, this installation plots the objects that represent their specific environment in another space with its own working class history at the Gesamkunstwerk Building.

> "This exhibition is dedicated to the tired and the weary- the ones that get up at the crack of dawn to drive the trucks, to stock the shelves, to pick the fruit, to make the things, to teach the children, to give the care, to punch a clock- day in, day out."
> 
> **—** Clara Varas

_Day In, Day Out_ is funded by The Ellies, Miami’s visual arts awards, presented by Oolite Arts.

[**Everything That Remains**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#everything-that-remains)

06\. 27 – 07\. 31. 2021

- Jee Park

Spinello Projects is proud to present _Everything that Remains_, the debut solo gallery exhibition by Korean-born  Miami-based artist Jee Park. The exhibition, spanning two rooms, features a body of mixed media and fabric wall works created between 2017-2021. Exhibition on view at the Gesamtkunstwerk Building located at 2930 NW 7th Avenue, from June 27 — July 31, 2021 and by appointment only.

Jee Park’s works in the exhibition, Everything that Remains, were created in a process of remembrance. Three dimensional paintings hang in different states of undress on the walls. Garments and household fabrics are the medium loosely and tightly wrapped around exposed stretcher bars. These textiles refer to home life, family, people’s lives, things that live on our skin and that we touch. They are articles of human life itself. Over and over again they are bundled, stretched, stitched, flowing, draping, marked up, taped, and stapled. More specific fragments of lives lived appear amongst large swaths of fabric, like small clues into the lived experience of losing and mourning.

This exhibition is informed by the Suui, a traditional Korean  burial garment. The Suui is made of carefully woven hemp fabric and is used to dress the dearly departed. Suui is a symbol for a person’s final rite of passage. Different elements of the Suui, such as sleeves, string, and collars, appear in the works. Objects that otherwise would’ve been discarded after the people who used them pass away, are reserved as material in these works. A father’s tie, a bed sheet, a phone charger, all live on here. These outlying artifacts of a family, or of a tradition are collaged, painted, and marked over with coffee or paint, or with words that cycle through the mind during long hours of the night. Park’s intuitive abstract mark making is instigated by emotions of grief, anxiety, and remembrance. Acts of collecting, repurposing, and sewing became therapeutic in light of the lives lost in the global pandemic and to racial violence.

[**UNDERCURRENT**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#undercurrent)

03\. 03 – 05\. 15. 2021

- Ema Ri

Spinello Projects presents _UNDERCURRENT_, the debut solo gallery exhibition by emerging Cuban-American, queer artist Ema Ri. The exhibition, spanning three rooms and two floors, features a suite of drywall reliefs and wall skin pieces, both free hanging wall sculptures and interventions embedded into the gallery walls.

Walls are loaded objects themselves, yet often overlooked. They contain long portions of our lives, carrying and holding our most precious possessions, artworks, markings, cracks; the microscopic tracing of life: dirt, dust, warmth, memories. These things are inherent and hidden, but completely exposed.

Ema Ri’s works materially possess the walls, exposing organic patterns, shapes, and extensive representations of life through excised paint, and plaster. Life is made of patterns, repeating shapes of perfect geometry/seemingly random and chaotic events. Ri takes hold of this when dissecting the interiors of drywall. Carving and meticulously exposing the inner world of what is supposed to become the inside of someone’s house, Ri contemplates the unseen relationships, communions, and felt impressions that everything and everyone experiences. By undermining these materials Ri marks lived spaces, like a timestamp for ideas. The walls come alive from the inside out.

Lines, spirals, waves and Rorschach-like symmetries carve out and peel away compositions that represent invisible flows inside and between us, pushing the material to its formal extremes. The negative and positive spaces relate what is here, now, and what was, as a mourning and acknowledgement of each other, our past, and loves lost. These works correlate to undercurrents that go unspoken and unknown in our lived experience and subconscious imagination. The question of, “if you see me, do you understand me?” circulates throughout the works but each piece contains its own visual language created by chiseling, plastering, braiding, folding, and peeling. Ema Ri’s exploration of the hidden or invisible by exposing the usually concealed parts of walls allow for contemplation and reflection.

[**FACING GAIA**](https://spinelloprojects.com/program/#facing-gaia)

03\. 03 – 05\. 15. 2021

- [Sinisa Kukec](https://spinelloprojects.com/artist/sinisa-kukec/)

Spinello Projects presents Sinisa Kukec’s, FACING GAIA, as a post process remnant of a communal cathartic performance or what Kukec calls, an act of “responsible inclusive violence”.

In their current state at Spinello Projects, the works in FACING GAIA are material reflections of the process of their conception. Kukec’s work is a reflection of its material, its environment, social outcomes, and behaviors or rituals. By stumbling upon FACING GAIA, you take part in it, either by peering into its surface, or by making a mark. Exhibition on view from March 3 — April 20, 2021 and by appointment only.

Inspired by the theory that claims that Earth is a self regulating system that intelligently and automatically reacts to everything happening to it, _FACING GAIA_ allowed its initial audience to pummel a polished aluminum monolith with granite stones laid at the site of their original installation at the Deering Estate. The gold polished aluminum surfaces of two monoliths exhibited are indented by a barrage of rock collisions and vandalistic engravings by visitors of the estate. The monoliths created a communal landmark to gather, and satisfyingly throw rocks at. Collective repetitive mark making transformed the reflective surface to create an organic dispersal pattern. Accompanying the Deering Estate monoliths, a suite of four small-scale works were made solo, in-studio. 

FACING GAIA was made possible by support from the Deering Estate and Spinello Projects.

**About the Deering Estate**

The [Deering Estate](https://deeringestate.org/) preserves the 1920s era Miami estate of Charles Deering, Chicago industrialist, early preservationist, environmentalist, art collector, philanthropist and first chairman of the International Harvester Company. The Deering Estate is a 21st Century house museum, cultural and ecological field station, and a national landmark listed on the National Register of Historic Places, owned by the State of Florida and managed by Miami-Dade County Parks, Recreation and Open Spaces Department. The Deering Estate is located at 16701 SW 72nd Ave. in Miami.

_Cultural Arts Programming at the Deering Estate is made possible with the support of the Miami-Dade County Department of Cultural Affairs and the Cultural Affairs Council, the Miami-Dade County Mayor and Board of County Commissioners, and The Deering Estate Foundation, Inc._

### SARAHCROWN is a contemporary art gallery founded in 2022 in Tribeca, New York, building on the expertise and relationships developed through its namesake art advisory practice, established in 2013.

### The gallery represents emerging and established international artists, with a focus on Postwar and Contemporary Art.

### SARAHCROWN is dedicated to discovering new artistic talent, developing site-specific projects, and fostering critical discourse around contemporary art and curatorial practice. Alongside its exhibition program, the gallery works closely with private and corporate collectors, providing guidance in building, maintaining, and expanding art collections.

## Tangere

10.17.26 — 12.06.26

[HP Denham](https://lvl3official.com/hp-denham/) [Jade Yumang](https://lvl3official.com/jade-yumang/)

- [Facebook](http://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=http%3A%2F%2Flvl3official.com%2Ftangere%2F&t=Tangere%20-%20LVL3 'Facebook')

- [Tumblr](http://www.tumblr.com/share/link?url=http%3A%2F%2Flvl3official.com%2Ftangere%2F&name=Tangere%20-%20LVL3&description= 'Tumblr')

LVL3 is elated to announce the opening of **_Tangere_**, a two-person exhibition featuring the works of **[HP Denham](https://lvl3official.com/hp-denham/)** (Los Angeles, CA) and **[Jade Yumang](https://lvl3official.com/jade-yumang/)** (Chicago, IL) on Saturday, October 17th, 2026.

_Noli me tangere._ At the threshold of the real, the caress traces the no-man’s land between being and not-yet-being. It seeks the unreality that slips away from the light of the graspable, the reasonable, the sensible.

This threshold of unreality is where Denham and Yumang meet: corporeal forms are defamiliarized, transformed and abstracted through oil and thread, respectively, into assemblages that unmake totalizing assumptions and agreements about what bodies are and do.

_Touch me not._ Offer me not to the grasping altar of anticipation. Find me in the caress that searches and forages, that ceaselessly escapes its form toward a future never future enough.

**Opening Reception: Saturday, October 17th, 6-9 PM**. _Tangere_ will be on view until December 6th, 2026. 
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ 
This text is deeply inspired by Emmanuel Levinas’ _Totality and Infinity_ (1969).

[**Twelve Ten**](https://twelvetengallery.com/)

[Exhibitions](https://twelvetengallery.com/exhibitions) [Fairs](https://twelvetengallery.com/fairs) [News](https://twelvetengallery.com/news) [About](https://twelvetengallery.com/about) [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/twelvetengallery/)

**Noelle Africh** 
_NADA Miami 2026_

December 1st — 5th, 2026 
Ice Palace Studios 
1400 North Miami Avenue 
[Inquire](mailto:joshua@twelvetengallery.com?subject=NADA)

Twelve Ten Gallery is pleased to present a solo booth of paintings by Chicago-based artist Noelle Africh. Africh's paintings explore the emergence of form through the material and historical properties of distemper, recasting one of the earliest painting media in conversation with modern forms of image making. Drawing from a diverse array of influences, including early photographic experimentation, material and process based-art, Africh develops the medium and its mnemonic content, affecting the moment where recognition is retroactively constituted.

Noelle Africh, "Privacy", 2026. Distemper on linen over panel. 12 x 9 in (22.86 x 20.48 cm). Photo credit: Jonas Mueller.

Consisting of chalk, pigment, and a binder, distemper is a medium that is applied while hot and fluid, undergoing a continual process of change as it cools and cures. The artist engages this alchemical flux, intervening with experimental techniques that reactivate the surface and alter its contingent outcomes. Latent images become visible through a material reaction, as though developed rather than composed. In this respect, Africh’s process recalls the temporal doubling of photographic processes, as the image is carefully calibrated in both its time of capture and time of exposure.

Africh’s images emerge mercurially through successive stages, the final form remaining unfixed until the artist marks their completion through an axiomatic decision. In this sense they draw on the rich dialectical arc between tradition and the avant-garde, as the determinate gestures of craft and authorial heroism are reconstituted in favor of autonomic execution and the selective framing of process and materials. The artist’s decision to arrest the process of a painting into one state, one moment, rather than another, demands a similarly nominative attention, their paintings occupying a space between the procedural and the intentional.

For Africh, this process of continuous change is where mimicry inspires mimesis. Recalling the work of post-minimalists such as Lynda Benglis or Eva Hesse, whose practices demonstrate how the literality of material acquires a new expressive relationship in regards to the body and time, Africh stages the synthetic constitution of memory. Their paintings foreground the act of recognition itself: the moment when a particular form may surface or be submerged within an indeterminate field.

For NADA Miami 2026, this focused presentation will bring together a selection of recent works that highlight Africh’s singular engagement with material transformation and the representational possibilities of painting’s surface.

Noelle Africh (b. 1992, Chicago, IL) lives and works in Chicago, IL. They received an MFA in Painting and Drawing from The School of the Art Institute of Chicago and a Bachelor of Science degree in Mathematics from the University of Illinois in Urbana-Champaign. Solo exhibitions include "Signal", Twelve Ten (Chicago, IL), "Superstition", Slow Dance (Chicago, IL) and "Loomer", SHED Projects (Cleveland, OH). They have also participated in a three-person at No31 (Duns, Scotland) in 2026, and many group exhibitions including at Galerie Gisela Clement (Bonn, Germany), RUSCHWOMAN (Chicago, IL), Hyde Park Art Center (Chicago, IL), The Plan (Chicago, IL), The Green Gallery - West (Milwaukee, WI), and Patient Info (Chicago, IL), among others.

### Cavin-Morris Gallery has been exhibiting contemporary artists from around the world for almost 40 years. We specialize in the work of artists who do not intentionally make art for the art world mainstream canon. We represent past and new generations of artists whose work ultimately feels timeless to us.

### We show an eclectic selection of tribal art from all the major regions of the world, focusing on the unusual and the formally surprising, focusing on the arts of masking.

### We also concentrate on both functional and non-functional contemporary ceramics. We are especially interested in the way certain ceramists push the envelope in their expression of traditional forms and cultures. We show work by Western ceramic artists, as well as works by artists from Japan, Korea, and China.

### The common thread that connects all this art is its uniqueness, its integrity, visionary authenticity, and its reflection of cultural homeground. We look for the place where labels become irrelevant and the work remains urgent, immediate, and singular.

## Fine Art Dealing, 
Advising, and Appraisals

---

AH Arts is a fine art gallery and boutique full-service advisory firm founded by [Alix Holloway](https://ahartsllc.com/about-alix), specializing in Modern, Post-War, and Contemporary Art that provides new and veteran collectors with the expertise, access, and education to build meaningful collections. Serving as both a secondary market dealer and trusted advisor, our mission is to source the right works for each client and offer them at the best price. To do that, we listen - to the interests of our clients, and the expertise of established scholars - we look (and keep looking), then, we act. 

With a commitment to integrity, transparency, and the highest ethical standards, AH Arts is a resource to help clients navigate the global art market by sourcing, and researching rare works of art to meet specific collecting goals or aesthetics. We welcome the challenge to find specific paintings, sculptures, or works on paper not previously presented on the market and work to bring them right to your door. We believe, even in this time of social distancing, nothing can replace seeing a work of art in person and connecting one-on-one with a trusted advocate to better understand the work. 

At AH Arts, we perform thorough market analysis and due diligence to illuminate an otherwise opaque industry to guide, educate and protect collectors for a meaningful and enjoyable collecting experience rooted in history, while designed to meet the needs of our time.

## HISTORY

Robert Miller Gallery was established in 1977 to encourage the reappraisal of underrepresented voices in contemporary art and provide a platform for a critical re-thinking of the 20th century canon. Over the years, the gallery has established an international reputation by working directly with some of the most important and influential artists of the last three decades including Yayoi Kusama, Ai Wei Wei, Louise Bourgeois, David Hockney, Leon Kossoff, Lee Krasner, Patti Smith, Robert Mapplethorpe, Joan Mitchell, Alice Neel, Georgia O’Keeffe, Andy Warhol, and Tom Wesselmann, and with the estates of Diane Arbus, Eva Hesse and Jean-Michel Basquiat.

Today the gallery continues to promote the careers of underrepresented, mid-career, and established artists; build public and private collections; organize significant exhibitions with other galleries; and facilitate museum shows and scholarly publications.

Many of these artists are currently on view in the in the Museum of Fine Arts (MFAH) inaugural exhibitions in the new Nancy and Rich Kinder Building.

metadata.title: Moeller Fine Art
metadata.description: Achim Moeller has been an art dealer, advisor, and appraiser since 1965. For the past 55 years he has specialized in 19th and 20th Century European and 20th Century American Masters, making Moeller Fine Art the foremost gallery in the United States for works by German Expressionists and the Masters of the Bauhaus. He has sold major works by Max Beckmann, Ernst Ludwig Kirchner, Erich Heckel, Max Pechstein, Karl Schmidt-Rottluff, Otto Mueller, Franz Marc, August Macke, Alexej von Jawlensky, Wassily Kandinsky, Paul Klee, Lyonel Feininger, among others to institutions including the Art Institute of Chicago, the Folkwang Museum, Essen, the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, the Museum Ludwig, Cologne, the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., the National Gallery of Canada, Ottawa, the Tate Gallery, London and the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Museums and collectors in the United States and Europe frequently consult Moeller to obtain appraisals for works in their collections for exhibition, insurance, and estate purposes. In 2014, Moeller announced the launch of the Moeller Art Advisory and Curatorial Service, which provides independent advice to present and future clients in their art collecting. Moeller Fine Art is currently a member of the Art Dealers Association of America (ADAA), the Syndicat des Négociants en Art (SNA) in France, the Confédération Internationale des Négociants en Œuvres d’Art (CINOA), and the International Fine Print Dealers Association (IFPDA). Moeller is also the internationally recognized authority on the life and work of Lyonel Feininger (1871–1956) and Mark Tobey (1890–1976). He is the author of Lyonel Feininger: The Catalogue Raisonné of Paintings and maintains the archives of both artists as the managing principal of The Lyonel Feininger Project LLC and The Mark Tobey Project LLC. He frequently provides expert opinions and, when appropriate, certificates of authenticity to collectors, dealers, auction houses, and museums. For over 30 years, Moeller was the curator and the sole advisor of the Hon. John C. Whitehead, former co-chairman of Goldman Sachs and Deputy Secretary of State (US), whose collection of late 19th and early 20th century French masters has been exhibited in top institutions around the world. Moeller has published numerous exhibition catalogues and is often retained as an exhibition consultant by museums both in the United States and abroad. Publications include, “ The Enchanted World of Lyonel Feininger”, "Paul Klee: Early and Late Years, 1894–1940" and "Lyonel Feininger: Drawings and Watercolors from the Julia Feininger Estate,"[5] and edited various publications such as "Years of Friendship: The Correspondence of Lyonel Feininger and Mark Tobey."[6] Moeller served as a consultant for the retrospective exhibition "Lyonel Feininger: At the Edge of the World"[7] at the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York, and the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts. Moeller Fine Art regularly exhibited at Art Basel, Art Cologne and the Armory Show. Moeller is a member of Rotary International, the American Council on Germany, the International Fine Print Dealers Association (IFPDA), the Catalogue Raisonné Scholars Association (CRS), the Honor Committee of Archivio Piero Dorazio, and the Friends of the Busch-Reisinger Museum, Harvard. Moeller opened his own gallery in London in 1972, and became a member of the Society of London Art Dealers in 1977. In 1984, he moved the gallery to New York and opened a Berlin location in 2009 under the direction of his daughter, Ms. Stephanie Moeller. The New York City gallery, Moeller Fine Art, is located at 7 East 60th Street.

metadata.description: Founded by Ales Ortuzar in 2018, Ortuzar is a gallery in Tribeca dedicated to promoting artists who have played a significant role in the development of 20th and 21st-century art but have not recently received critical exposure in New York. Ortuzar presents exhibitions in collaboration with artists, estates, foundations, and representing galleries, with the goal of providing expanded visibility and fostering renewed interest in artists’ work.

about us

**instituto de visión** is a gallery focused on conceptual practices, directed by women and located in Bogotá. Our mission is to investigate the artistic discourses that have been left out of the official history of art. Through the [**{ visionarios }**](https://institutodevision.com/es/visionaries/) program, we have recovered important collections of the Latin American art scene from the mid-20th century and we continue to investigate the most enigmatic praxis in the region.

Through a double program, we also represent some of the most relevant practices in Mexico, Chile, North America, Venezuela, among others. Led by three women, the **instituto de visión** pays special attention to female voices, queer theory, environmental activism, the displaced condition, and other critical positions that challenge the established order.

Using the international art scene as a platform, we are committed to giving visibility and expanding the work of artists who reveal critical realities and raise important questions to understand contemporary issues.

Directora de producción y Cofundadora

## ( Colombia )

# Karen Abreu

Historiadora del arte del UCL y SOAS London. Interesada en la producción artesanal tradicional y las materias primas de origen natural dentro del discurso artístico contemporáneo. Su experiencia en producción cinematográfica aporta al desarrollo técnico, museístico y conceptual. 
\- 
Art historian from UCL and SOAS London.Her interest revolves around traditional artisan production and the raw materials of natural origin within contemporary artistic discourse. Her experience in film production is a tool to successfully exhibitions at a technical, museum and conceptual level.

Directora artisticas y Cofundadora / Artistic director and Co-founder

## ( Colombia )

# Beatríz López

Curadora y galerista residente en Nueva York. Su trabajo se cuestiona las relaciones de poder en procesos de colonización, Enfocándolo en las narrativas relacionadas con el arte, la naturaleza, el cuerpo y la revisión de las mujeres en la historia oficial del arte del siglo XX en Colombia. 
\- 
Curator and gallery owner based in New York. His work question the relations generated from colonization processes. she has focused on narratives concerning the relationship between art, body nature and the revision of women in the official history of art in the 20th century in Colombia.

Directora ejecutiva y Cofundadora / Executive director and Co-founder

## ( Colombia )

# Omayra Alvarado

Vive en los Angeles CA. Su trabajo se enfoca en fortalecer la practica de los artistas en el mercado internacional. Sus intereses conceptuales se estructuran a partir de obras seminales y ejes formales que dan coherencia a colecciones privadas e institucionales. 
\- 
Lives in Los Angeles CA. Her work focuses on strengthening the practice of artists in the international market. Her conceptual interests are structured from seminal works and formal axes that give coherence to private and institutional collections.

Asistente de dirección / Director´s assistant

## ( Colombia )

# Sandra Lucía Caicedo

[sandrac@institutodevision.com](mailto:sandrac@institutodevision.com)

# Un pozo que mira al cielo

artistas: [Santiago Reyes Villaveces](https://institutodevision.com/artists/santiago-reyes-villaveces/)

Saturday 19 September, 2026 — Tuesday 29 September, 2026

Un pozo que mira al cielo brings together works by Santiago Reyes Villaveces that connect space and the body with forces that do not appear directly as images: magnetism, the underground, and scales that exceed the human. Rather than representing these forces, the exhibition operates as a sensory apparatus that excavates, conducts, displaces, suspends, and illuminates. Science and sculpture intersect through concrete operations that reorganize matter, architecture, and the body. At this intersection, the exhibition intertwines the subterranean and the orbital within the body of those who move through it.

A magnetic mass functions as a core; around it, rods trace orbits, returns, and tensions. It is the anatomy of a field. An inscription warns that people with pacemakers should not approach. The warning makes explicit that the field affects bodies and devices, organizes distances, and transforms the relationship with those who come near it.

In magnetism, there are no isolated poles. Every magnetic field closes back upon itself. It does not begin or end at a single point: it circulates. North and south are opposing moments within the same flow. When a magnet is broken, each fragment produces its own system of polarity. The break reproduces the relationship it sought to divide. Magnetism thus emerges as an active relation between scales: what acts between fragments also traverses planetary bodies.

( [bogotá](https://institutodevision.com/exhibitions/) )

# Online Exhibition - William Hogarth, Select Prints: A Private Collection

It is not an overstatement to characterize William Hogarth as pioneering and revolutionary. For his time he was avant-garde, cutting-edge, and shocking in his depiction of audacious subject matter. Trained as both a printmaker and painter, it was his prints that enabled him to reach and scandalize a domestic and international audience. Several series of his etchings – in particular, _A Rake’s Progress, A Harlot’s Progress, Marriage à la Mode and Gin Street, Beer Lane_ – moralized, titillated, and with their massive popularity and commercial success brought Hogarth and English art its first widespread recognition beyond England’s own shores.

The material in this catalogue is the complete private collection of Hogarth prints formed by a discerning American collector, Herbert M. Schiller, M.D. Dr. Schiller did most of his buying in the 1990’s in London. The major sets and most of the major individual prints are represented.

## NOMAD Abu Dhabi

18 November–22 November 2026Abu Dhabi

Carpenters’ inaugural participation in NOMAD Abu Dhabi features a booth combining functional, conceptual and collectible design. Through works featuring sculpture, lighting, ceramics and other mediums, the display presents over 15 artists and designers from the gallery’s global roster to collectors, curators and cultural leaders attending the annual fair in the UAE that offers dialogue and exchange between art, architecture and design.
